summary: 36-year-old woman, day 6 after open appendicectomy for perforated appendicitis: red, fluctuant wound with pus, erythema 2 cm, T 37.6°C, HR 88.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Red painful wound leaking pus after operation
inputs.hpi: Open (gridiron) appendicectomy 6 days ago for perforated appendicitis; discharged day 3 on oral antibiotics, finished yesterday. Wound increasingly painful and red for 2 days, pus from the lateral end today. Eating normally, bowels open, no vomiting, no abdominal pain away from the wound.

exam.general: Well. HR 88, BP 122/78, RR 16, SpO2 99% on air, T 37.6°C.
exam.abdomen: Right iliac fossa wound: erythema 2 cm beyond the edges, fluctuant, purulent discharge from the lateral end. Abdomen otherwise soft and non-tender.
exam.skin: Erythema 2 cm around the incision, no crepitus, no necrosis.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Superficial incisional surgical site infection — day 6 after open appendicectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Superficial incisional SSI with a small wound abscess; no systemic features, erythema <5 cm. Open and drain the wound, swab, dressings; antibiotics only if cellulitis spreads or systemic signs.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage emergency_now (score 88): 'Post-operative concern' (urgent) for 'wound … pus' wording, plus 'Vomiting or possible dehydration' from the negated 'no vomiting'.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Post-operative ward reviews: score post-op concern from physiology (NEWS2) rather than adding 'Post-operative concern' (urgent) for any 'post-op'/'wound' word; reserve emergency_now for physiological or peritonitic criteria.

mustExclude.note: No broad-spectrum IV antibiotics for a superficial SSI without systemic signs.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE NG125 — Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment
guideline.section: 1.3 Antibiotic prophylaxis before clean surgery involving a prosthesis or implant, clean-contaminated and contaminated surgery; single dose IV on starting anaesthesia; do not use routinely for clean non-prosthetic uncomplicated surgery; take allergy and local resistance into account. 1.4 SSI treatment: antibiotic covering likely organisms, local resistance and culture results
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment (NG125). London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2020).

guideline.name: IDSA practice guideline — skin and soft tissue infections (surgical site infections)
guideline.section: Suture removal plus incision and drainage for SSI; antibiotics added only with systemic signs (T >38.5 °C, HR >110) or erythema/induration extending >5 cm; after intestinal surgery cover gram-negatives and anaerobes
guideline.citation: Stevens DL, Bisno AL, Chambers HF, et al. Clin Infect Dis. 2014;59:e10–52.

rationale: Permutation: superficial SSI after appendicectomy (so an appendicectomy template would be a repeat-operation error). Tests diagnosis, wound drainage, swab, triage level and antibiotic restraint.
